newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bankgesellschaft denies BfG takeover report.
newsitem.headline: Bankgesellschaft denies BfG takeover report.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG on Wednesday denied a report in a German newsletter that it was in talks to take over BfG Bank from its cash-hungry French parent, Credit Lyonnais.
"There are no such talks taking place," said a Bankgesellschaft spokeswoman. "And I am not aware of any in the past."

Platow Brief newsletter had said Bankgesellschaft wanted to buy BfG to expand its West German business and offset its problems in the eastern states while Credit Lyonnais needed to sell BfG to raise funds ahead of its privatisation.

BfG, one of the larger German second-tier banks, also dismissed the report. A spokesman said the bank was unaware of any plans to sell it to Bankgesellschaft, although he conceded that such a move might have been considered.
Credit Lyonnais has consistently denied any interest in selling BfG, in which it acquired a majority stake in late 1992, although analysts have noted a weakening of those denials in recent times.
Sources in Frankfurt banking circles said the sale of BfG might be viewed as attractive at first sight but would raise practical problems.
In the first place Credit Lyonnais was still viewed as unlikely to want to part with its BfG stake, which has given it a strong position in Germany.

In addition, BfG's other major shareholders, the BGAG trade union holding and insurance group AMB Holding, could pose significant difficulties, since these can demand that BfG only be sold as a complete unit, forcing CL to buy out their shares before proceeding with the sale, the sources said.

Bankgesellschaft, at the centre of speculation about a possible merger with Norddeutsche Landesbank, earlier this week said it had been forced to set aside 2.2 billion marks in provisions for problems loans this year, after a slump in the local economy.
